meta.title: Claude Software Factory: workflow, design choices, coverage
meta.subtitle: Nesting-dolls explorer of the software-factory repository

factory.title: Claude Software Factory
factory.summary: A set of skills, rules, deterministic gates and designed agent roles that turn an AI coding assistant from a 'vibe-coder' into a disciplined engineer: requirements are verified before use, tests come before code, the implementer is blind to the tests, and verification is deterministic and independent.
detail: The factory is three things layered together. The method (the /sf build loop, its skills and the new sf toolchain) runs today. A deterministic engine (the sf CLI) enforces test integrity, one-way-door detection and, through factory/verify, honest solver verdicts on a small pure subset. An agent layer (seven roles, eight hooks, generator, settings emitter, ledger, walking skeleton) is implemented and acceptance-tested but not yet exercised in a live Claude Code session.
Click any stacked box to open the diagram inside it. The Coverage tab lists what is built, partial, only designed, outside the repo, or a gap, with reasons.

design.choice: Guard one-way doors; leave two-way doors fast
design.why: Local, reversible work (UI, helpers, cache TTLs) runs autonomously; schemas, auth, public API and vector dimensions need a Socratic debate and an ADR.
design.alternatives: One uniform, rigid process for every change

design.choice: Verification is deterministic; models advise, they do not vote
design.why: Hash baselines, AST scans and hooks cannot be talked around, which is the answer to reward hacking.
design.alternatives: LLM committees grading each other's work

files.note: The manifesto and the two-door model
The research argument behind the design

coverage.note: The method, the sf CLI and tool groups, the agent layer (roles, generator, settings emitter, seven hooks, ledger, stage graph, walking skeleton), slices, intake, structure, contracts/solver, QA loop and dashboard are implemented and tested: 4,017 unit tests and 1,497 eval cases pass, golden gate 141 of 141. Live behaviour inside a real Claude Code session and cross-vendor review are not verified.
gaps: Hooks are mechanical only in projects where sf has generated the project settings; exercised through the command line and simulated event streams, not a live session (clarification C-34 is still open)
The Bash and blindness guards are command-text guards and cannot be complete; the OS sandbox is the backstop (see the residual-risk sections of docs/hooks/bash_guard.md and blindness_guard.md)
One acceptance case is open by design pending a decision: TB06-D-035 (docs/adr/ADR-0004)
The repository has a build-loop profile now (docs/development-workflow.md) but the factory is not yet run through its own loop for every change

intake.title: Requirements intake and sweep
intake.summary: Before any line of a brief becomes a requirement, it is transcribed verbatim, swept for traps (licences, provider terms, impossible guarantees, inverted rubrics), settled by research and experiments, and only then written into a PRD and a requirements ledger.
detail: Every line of prose in a source brief is a requirement, including 'optional' items and out-of-scope lists. The ledger is the one summary table allowed to exist because stage 9 of the loop rebuilds its touched rows from the source every time.

design.choice: Sweep the brief before trusting it
design.why: Briefs and rubrics can carry traps: a licence you cannot meet, a guarantee theory rules out, a rubric that rewards the wrong thing. Finding them after building is far more expensive.
design.alternatives: Trusting the PRD as written

design.choice: The sweep is a loop, not a one-shot gate
design.why: Suspects are settled with grounded research and experiments until the loop converges; the PRD is written only after.
design.alternatives: A single checklist pass

files.contains: Sweep the brief before trusting it
files.note: Stage 1 describes the minesweeper discovery loop

coverage.note: The skills exist outside this repo and the process is written into /sf; this repository only holds the design proposal.
gaps: The only in-repo document about the sweep still says 'Nothing is built yet', while an engine, 26 lens packs and tests exist under ~/.claude/skills/minesweeper

research-loop.summary: grounded-research verifies single claims, deep-research surveys a topic, and experiment-designer pre-registers a fair comparison when two or more approaches remain.

design.choice: Enumerate candidates from a dated source, never from recall
design.why: A list written from memory stops at the training cutoff; a committed enumeration lets a reader tell 'rejected' from 'never considered'.

prd-writer.summary: Writes the real PRD (work units with file scope, accepted ADRs, experiment verdicts) from the checked problem definition and the trap register.

req-ledger.title: Requirements ledger
req-ledger.summary: One row per requirement line with a status and the artifact that satisfies it or the dependency it waits on. It is what makes 'the run ends when requirements are met' measurable.

design.choice: Pick the next slice from the ledger, not from a queue
design.why: A queue is a guess at what the requirements need and runs out first; unserved rows with no producer are the highest-value work.

minesweeper.title: Minesweeper
minesweeper.summary: Sweeps a brief for traps with swappable lens packs, assigns deterministic severity, and hands a checked problem definition to the PRD writer.
detail: Lenses cover licence, provider terms, privacy, regulation, hallucinated dependencies, impossible guarantees, inverted rubrics and omitted trust or threat models. An open Critical finding blocks scheduling of the rows it conditions until the owner signs off.

design.choice: Modular lens packs
design.why: New domains and releases add a lens directory instead of rewriting the engine.
design.alternatives: One monolithic checklist

coverage.note: Installed with an engine, lens packs and tests; not catalogued here and its proposal document is stale. Its tests were not run in this exploration.
gaps: Proposal still says 'Nothing is built yet'

build-loop.title: Build loop (/sf)
build-loop.summary: The fixed twelve-stage loop every implementation slice follows, bound into a checklist with one todo per stage so a skipped stage is visible instead of forgotten.
detail: The loop is not a variable: schedule pressure may reorder or slice work smaller but never drop a stage. The run ends when every requirement line is satisfied or recorded as blocked with what it waits on, not when a queue empties.

design.choice: Make the back half of the loop a checklist
design.why: Research and experiments are interesting and get done; tests-first, blind implementation, separate runner, adversarial review and drift check cost time without visible progress, so they quietly vanish. A todo per stage makes a skip visible.
design.alternatives: A process document consulted from memory

coverage.note: Fully written and in daily use on other projects; absent for this repository itself.
gaps: The installed skill is the only copy: the repository's own history does not version it

adrs.title: Architecture decision records
adrs.summary: ADR-0001 chooses the Unity-IR dual-plane substrate, ADR-0002 the zero-trust verification substrate, ADR-0003 seven agent roles above skills.

design.choice: Unity-IR (ADR-0001)
design.why: A deterministic three-layer schema decouples reasoning from lexical syntax; reviewers audit semantic delta rather than lines.
design.alternatives: Raw polyglot source in the model context

design.choice: Zero-trust verification (ADR-0002)
design.why: Hashed baselines, design-by-contract and symbolic exploration remove reward hacking structurally.
design.alternatives: Trusting model-written tests

design.choice: Roles above skills (ADR-0003)
design.why: Split by context boundary, not pipeline phase; one writer per tree; hooks enforce, prompts advise.
design.alternatives: A fixed seven-stage relay

coverage.note: ADR-0001 to 0003 accepted; ADR-0004 (blindness guard and symlinks) is proposed and needs a decision.
gaps: deal and CrossHair from ADR-0002 are still unused by production code; the z3 solver gate in factory/verify covers a small pure subset

agent-layer.title: Agent layer
agent-layer.summary: Seven agent definitions (orchestrator, research, design, audit, implement, test, review) with their own models, tool allowlists and hooks, generated from a project profile so nothing names a specific project. Specified through 14 tracer-bullet PRDs; none implemented.
detail: Seven roles, eight hook ids, a profile loader, a stage graph, an agent file generator, a settings emitter, a tamper-evident ticket ledger and an end-to-end simulation with a shadow routing log exist as code, with 1,000+ acceptance cases behind them. Implementers were mechanically blind to the evals (sparse worktrees without evals/), and an independent runner graded each slice; QA feedback and the clarifications C-36 to C-39 record what the iterations found.

design.choice: Split by context boundary, not pipeline phase
design.why: Phase-based splits add coordination overhead and lost accuracy on sequential tasks.
design.alternatives: A seven-stage relay

design.choice: Everything project-specific comes from a profile
design.why: Roles, skills and hooks stay generic; the profile supplies paths, one-way-door patterns, deploy route.
design.alternatives: Per-project forks of the role files

coverage.note: All 14 tracer bullets are implemented by blind implementers and pass their acceptance cases after QA iterations; one diagnostic case is open pending ADR-0004.
gaps: TB06-D-035 open (ADR-0004); everything else green, golden 141 of 141
Not exercised in a real Claude Code session (C-34); command-text guards have documented residual risk

role-review.summary: Independent read of the diff, traces and passes; drift against requirements. Read-only; verdict only.
detail: Proposed model: A different vendor from Implement where available.
Verdict must be APPROVE or REJECT with citations.

coverage.note: Role data is loaded and validated and a generated agent file can be emitted from it; model choices remain proposals to measure.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.summary: Seven deterministic hook specs share one core: a payload parser and decision type, then guards for paths, blindness, secrets, Bash, stop and sub-agent stop. Guards fail closed on malformed input.

design.choice: Hooks enforce; prompts advise
design.why: Each 'must never' is a hook or a missing tool, so an agent cannot talk its way past it.
design.alternatives: Instructions in the role prompt

design.choice: Hooks are pure decision functions with a thin protocol adapter
design.why: No network, no model call, easy to test with recorded payloads.
design.alternatives: Hooks that call a model to judge

coverage.note: Eight hook ids are implemented behind one registry; every guard has acceptance cases; security-review hardening recorded as clarifications C-36 to C-39.

hook-core.title: Hook core
hook-core.summary: A frozen Payload dataclass, a Decision type (allow, deny, ask) and a thin adapter that turns stdin JSON into a decision and exit code; the command-line shape every hook shares.

coverage.note: Implemented from the published contract by a blind implementer. Acceptance cases for this slice all pass (evals/agents); the blind implementer never saw them.

path-guard.title: Path guard
path-guard.summary: Each role may write only its own folders (Research under research/, Design under docs/prd, spec and adr, Audit under docs/audit, Review nowhere). Only Implement writes application code.

coverage.note: Implemented; hardened after automated security review (clarification C-38: awk, sed, git abbreviations, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit). Acceptance cases for this slice all pass (evals/agents); the blind implementer never saw them.
gaps: Command-text parsing cannot be complete: the OS sandbox is the backstop (docs/hooks/path_guard.md)

secrets-guard.title: Secrets guard
secrets-guard.summary: For every agent, blocks Write, Edit and Bash content containing a key-shaped value (sk-ant-, ghp_, private-key headers); allows references by variable name.

coverage.note: Implemented; hardened after security review (C-39: whole-value placeholders, bounded scanning, de-quoted Bash scan). Acceptance cases for this slice all pass (evals/agents); the blind implementer never saw them.
gaps: A key split by shell quoting is caught only when the value has a known key shape

bash-guard.title: Bash guard
bash-guard.summary: Blocks git add -A and add ., --no-verify, force push, amend and rebase without approval; asks a human before destructive SQL, resource deletion, any deploy and every profile one-way-door pattern.

coverage.note: Implemented; wrapper options are parsed from tables and anything unclassifiable fails closed; su, runuser, doas, ssh and similar wrappers are never unwrapped (always ask or deny). Acceptance cases for this slice all pass (evals/agents); the blind implementer never saw them.
gaps: Not a complete defence: shell-style git aliases, xargs and find -exec chains, variables set outside the command; the OS sandbox is the backstop

stop-gate.title: Stop gate
stop-gate.summary: Refuses 'done' from Implement if a test was skipped, xfailed, deleted or given a trivial assertion, a frozen test's hash changed, or there is no evidence of a full-suite run.

coverage.note: Implemented from the published contract by a blind implementer. Acceptance cases for this slice all pass (evals/agents); the blind implementer never saw them.

subagent-validators.title: Sub-agent validators
subagent-validators.summary: At SubagentStop: Research must have a sources section and mark unverified claims; Audit rows need file, line and severity; Review verdict must be APPROVE or REJECT with citations.

coverage.note: Implemented from the published contract by a blind implementer. Acceptance cases for this slice all pass (evals/agents); the blind implementer never saw them.

blindness-guard.title: Blindness guard
blindness-guard.summary: For the implement agent only, denies Read, Grep, Glob and Bash commands that reference eval or held-out paths, including indirect forms. Every other role is never affected.

design.choice: Block by hook on agent_type, not by prompt instruction
design.why: A PreToolUse payload carries agent_type, so one shared hook can block a path for one agent only.
design.alternatives: Read(evals/**) permission deny alone, which does not stop shell reads

coverage.note: Implemented and tightened over several QA and security iterations; all but one acceptance case pass.
gaps: TB06-D-035 open: Glob through a symlink (docs/adr/ADR-0004)
Run-time-built file names, interpreter internals and other checkouts remain documented residual gaps

bi-paths.title: Protected paths
bi-paths.summary: paths.eval and paths.held_out from the profile, never hard-coded; a path is protected after normalising against cwd, collapsing . and .., and resolving symlinks.

coverage.note: Implemented in factory/hooks/blindness_guard.py; unit tests and acceptance cases pass.

bi-direct.title: Read, Grep, Glob
bi-direct.summary: Deny a protected file_path, and deny a Grep or Glob whose path is missing, '.', or a strict ancestor of a protected path, telling the agent to search a specific subfolder instead.

coverage.note: Implemented in factory/hooks/blindness_guard.py; unit tests and acceptance cases pass.

bi-bash.title: Bash commands
bi-bash.summary: Deny commands that name a protected path in any argument form, run recursive searches that would reach it, or use interpreter one-liners; allow ordinary builds, tests of the agent's own directories, git diff and ls src.

coverage.note: Implemented in factory/hooks/blindness_guard.py; unit tests and acceptance cases pass.

bi-indirect.title: Indirect forms
bi-indirect.summary: Relative, absolute, parent (../), quoted, glob (ev*/, **/evals), tilde and $VAR forms that could expand to a protected path.

coverage.note: Implemented in factory/hooks/blindness_guard.py; unit tests and acceptance cases pass.

bi-limits.title: Known limits
bi-limits.summary: A permissions.deny rule applies to sub-agents and best-effort to Grep and Glob, but does not stop a shell command or script that reads the files without naming them. The sandbox is the OS-level backstop.

coverage.note: An acknowledged residual hole with no mitigation in the guard: the sandbox is the backstop.
gaps: File names built at run time, awk/editor internals, git diff of revisions, other checkouts are documented as accepted residual risk

verification-engine.title: Verification engine (sf CLI)
verification-engine.summary: A small deterministic Python package behind the sf command: it classifies architectural doors, locks test baselines against reward hacking, runs a gated synthesis loop around the Claude CLI, and transpiles with a proved equivalence. About 2,000 lines.

design.choice: Bare-metal CLI over a framework
design.why: A lightweight Python runner that shells out to the local claude CLI; sub-70 ms invariant checks.
design.alternatives: A heavier orchestration service

coverage.note: The sf engine is implemented and tested with Unity installed (4,017 tests pass in the bounded full run); governance now fails closed and the CLI exposes the new tool groups.
gaps: The semantic verifier is Unity, which an earlier audit found ledger-specific; this was not re-run here. The new honest solver gate for a pure subset is factory/verify (sf contracts)
tests marked requires_unity need the sibling Unity repo; CI runs the rest
One intermittent failure of the transpiler parity test was seen once and not explained

sf-cli.title: sf CLI
sf-cli.summary: Argparse entry point with four subcommands: audit, verify, run and transpile; installed as sf and as a backward-compatible factory alias.

coverage.note: audit, verify, run, transpile plus the tool groups slice, structure, contracts, intake, ops and qa.

governance.title: Governance engine
governance.summary: Classifies a change as a one-way or two-way door from the semantic delta and source patterns (lock removal, purity loss, contract violation, public API, schema, auth boundary, symbol removal) and drafts an ADR.

design.choice: Two door types with eight risk categories
design.why: ONE_WAY means irreversible with high blast radius and requires debate and an ADR; TWO_WAY runs autonomously.
design.alternatives: A single severity score

coverage.note: A missing or crashing verifier now returns GATE FAILED (exit 3), never a harmless classification; pattern-only analysis is labelled UNVERIFIED.
gaps: Semantic classification still depends on Unity being installed

zero-trust.title: Zero-trust substrate
zero-trust.summary: Locks pre-existing tests by SHA-256 baseline manifest and parses the AST to catch reward hacking: dropped assertion counts, injected skip or xfail, and trivial assertions such as assert True.

design.choice: Hash the tests, scan the AST, do not ask a model
design.why: Reward hacking by an agent that writes both code and tests is caught structurally.
design.alternatives: LLM judging whether tests were weakened

coverage.note: The hash and AST guard is implemented; the formal-proof half promised by ADR-0002 now lives in factory/verify (z3) rather than here.
gaps: ZeroTrustGate still accepts contract_violations that synthesis never supplies
deal and CrossHair are not used by production code

transpiler.title: Polyglot transpiler
transpiler.summary: Synthesizes a cross-lingual anchor (for example Python to Go) and claims a certified zero semantic delta between source and target.

coverage.note: Implemented; tests pass with Unity installed; one intermittent failure seen once.
gaps: Needs the Unity compiler

claude-cli.title: Claude Code CLI
claude-cli.summary: The synthesis step shells out to claude -p with --restricted, which removes the built-in tools that run commands or code, so the call produces text only.

coverage.note: Verified against this machine's claude --help: --restricted exists.

unity-ir.title: Unity-IR compiler
unity-ir.summary: A sibling repository that lowers code to a canonical three-layer IR and computes semantic delta with Z3. Optional at runtime: the governance engine falls back to patterns when it is missing.

coverage.note: Separate repository, pinned in pyproject.toml to a developer's absolute path.

synthesis.title: Synthesis engine
synthesis.summary: Gathers context, asks the Claude CLI for a candidate patch, stages it atomically, and accepts it only if three deterministic gates pass; otherwise it rolls back and retries with the failure as feedback, up to three times.

design.choice: Atomic staging with backups and rollback
design.why: A rejected candidate leaves the tree exactly as it found it.
design.alternatives: Applying patches in place and fixing forward

design.choice: Deterministic gates, then self-repair
design.why: Failure text from a gate, not model self-assessment, drives the next attempt.
design.alternatives: Asking the model if its patch is good

coverage.note: The loop is implemented with tests; one governance-rejection test needs Unity. The Claude call has a 600 s timeout and no cost accounting.

syn-context.title: Gather context
syn-context.summary: Reads target source files, lowers them to Unity-IR where possible, and collects baseline test files and their hashes.

coverage.note: Implemented.

syn-candidate.title: Candidate patch
syn-candidate.summary: Builds the prompt (spec, context, previous failure feedback) and calls the local claude CLI in restricted mode, so it returns text and takes no actions.

coverage.note: Implemented; a dry-run mode skips the call.

syn-stage.title: Stage atomically
syn-stage.summary: Parses the response into file patches, records original contents as backups, then writes the new files.

coverage.note: Implemented.

syn-gate1.title: Gate 1: governance
syn-gate1.summary: Compares each changed non-test source file with its original; any ONE_WAY risk rejects the candidate and rolls back with the risk descriptions as feedback.

coverage.note: Works; its test needs the Unity compiler to detect lock removal.

syn-gate2.title: Gate 2: zero-trust
syn-gate2.summary: Verifies the baseline manifest and original test contents: deleted, weakened or skipped assertions reject the candidate.

coverage.note: Implemented; contract violations are never fed in.

syn-gate3.title: Gate 3: run the tests
syn-gate3.summary: Runs the project's test suite on the staged tree; failure feeds the last 1,500 characters of output back as feedback.

coverage.note: Implemented.

syn-repair.title: Rollback and retry
syn-repair.summary: Atomically restores backups and loops with the gate's failure text; after max_retries (default 3) returns a failure result with the last feedback.

coverage.note: Implemented.

syn-receipt.title: Receipt
syn-receipt.summary: On success returns modified files, iteration count and a generated receipt of what was done.

coverage.note: Implemented.

evals-gate.title: Evals and golden gate
evals-gate.summary: Evals are authored from published contracts before any implementer exists, then locked. 1,302 cases (129 golden must-pass, 1,173 diagnostic) all resolve to 'blocked' until something implements them; an independent audit found the golden gate not collectively exhaustive.

design.choice: A case written early resolves to blocked, never pass
design.why: lib.need() imports the producer; if it is missing the case is blocked, so a skeleton cannot earn a green.
design.alternatives: Skipping cases until the feature exists

design.choice: Golden membership is locked in GOLDEN.json
design.why: run.py requires the golden-tagged set to equal the list exactly; changing it is a reviewed baseline update.

coverage.note: 1,498 cases (golden 141): 1,496 pass, 1 open diagnostic (TB06-D-035), 1 library self-check blocked by design. The golden gate is GREEN. The five audit P0 findings are closed; C-38 and C-39 added cases.
gaps: TB06-D-035 is open pending ADR-0004
Results are gitignored (evals/agents/results/)

routing.title: Jev routing (shadow)

design.choice: Shadow mode only
design.why: Thresholds are placeholders until our own labelled past tasks set them; decisions are logged beside the real choice to build that data.
design.alternatives: Letting the classifier route from day one

design.choice: Deterministic rules first, a typed classifier second
design.why: Rules that are cheap and exact run before any model call; a Jev fault is recorded, never raised.
design.alternatives: Model-only routing

coverage.note: Client, policy and recorded-response tests exist.
gaps: Not wired into anything (promotion ledger)
Endpoint is an alpha API; thresholds are placeholders
Requires an OpenRouter key at run time

intake-gate.title: Intake gate
intake-gate.summary: Ledger with one row per source line and a trust column, a recorded minesweeper sweep per source hash, a gate that fails when the sweep did not run, an open Critical has no sign-off or a High has no disposition, plus checks for research seeds and experiment records.

coverage.note: Implemented and tested (61 tests). The sweep and the value-extraction pass are model procedure; only recording and gating are deterministic.

slice-format.title: Slice format
slice-format.summary: docs/slices/<id>/ with UX stories first, public acceptance criteria with IDs, a two-state task list (implemented by the implementer, verified only by QA), a criteria lock and an additive-only amendment log; checker, triage and a completion gate.

structure-scan.title: Structure scan
structure-scan.summary: stdlib ast extraction of symbols, imports and calls with stable ids and spans; edges labelled resolved, syntactic or unresolved with a reason; bounded scope; symbol diff by normalised AST hash; output becomes a dolls model that the checker verifies.

coverage.note: Implemented and tested (34 tests); run on this repo's own factory/ package.

Independent adversarial acceptance is in progress

contract-verify.title: Contracts and solver
contract-verify.summary: Independent contracts for pure int/bool functions with IDs, frame conditions and assumptions; contract review before code; z3 verification of the real implementation with PROVED, COUNTEREXAMPLE (replayed on the real function), UNSUPPORTED (routed), UNKNOWN and TIMEOUT; fails closed; counterexamples become regression tests.

design.choice: Replay every counterexample on the real function
design.why: If z3 and Python disagree the translator is wrong; that is MODEL_MISMATCH and fails the gate.
design.alternatives: Trusting the solver model

coverage.note: Implemented and tested (152 tests plus a differential test of the z3 model against real Python); demonstrated end to end on a labelled minimal fixture (examples/dogfood-limits).
gaps: Supported subset only: no loops, calls, floats or containers; everything else must route to tests
int64 is modelled as checked overflow, not wraparound
Generated regression tests replay an absolute source path
Independent adversarial acceptance is in progress

blind-worktree.title: Blind worktree
blind-worktree.summary: scripts/implementer-worktree.sh creates a worktree with protected paths absent (sparse checkout), a local Read deny rule, and cleans up if any step fails.

coverage.note: Tested (7 tests); used for every blind implementer in this build.
gaps: The object database still holds the protected files: a shell command could read them from git; the hooks and sandbox are the backstop

qa-loop.title: QA loop
qa-loop.summary: State per slice, a failure signature, a bounded retry policy with measured escalation, behavioural feedback guarded by a leak check against protected material, regression proposals, and a reviewer hand-off; QA alone marks tasks verified.

coverage.note: Implemented and tested (79 tests including a scripted fake-implementer simulation); policy defaults are configurable and tuned from recorded attempts.
gaps: Not yet run against real agent sessions
Tamper detection misses someone who rewrites the logs and the state together

ops-dashboard.title: Dashboard
ops-dashboard.summary: factory.ops bundles historical development artifacts per commit from the git object database into content-addressed blobs, collects runtime telemetry separately with measured / not-measured labels, and a static shell offers a commit selector and tabs.

coverage.note: Built and tested (27 + 8 tests); verified in a real browser against this repository's history.
gaps: Not deployed
Runtime telemetry covers only what its config declares; most figures are 'not measured' without configuration
Langfuse and CI figures are reported only when configured

resource-limits.title: Resource limits
resource-limits.summary: Repo-root conftest.py caps address space and per-test time; scripts/bounded-pytest.sh adds a wall-clock kill, a lock and a limits log. Added after a 19 GB runaway test killed a session.

coverage.note: Tested (4 tests); every test run since the incident used it.
gaps: A tripped limit is a failure, not a pass; a limit that is too tight would need tuning

native-install.title: Native install
native-install.summary: sf install writes the generated agents, settings-level hooks with absolute verified commands, the Sonnet-only pin and a manifest into a project; doctor executes every hook command (a hook that cannot run fails open); uninstall restores from backups.

coverage.note: Implemented and unit-tested (35 tests); verified in real headless Claude Code sessions: skills, agents and hooks resolve, hooks block in subagents, the pin overrides an inherited default (docs/native-verification/2026-10-19/REPORT.md).
gaps: Interactive (non -p) use not exercised
The user-level default model (Opus) is deliberately unchanged; sessions elsewhere without --model sonnet or a project pin still inherit it
A hook parser guard is not OS isolation

human-stop.title: Human stop
human-stop.summary: sf hitl request/status/release: a hash-chained stop ledger under .factory/stops that sf slice done and sf qa next obey; release needs a person at a terminal and the release command is a one-way door.

coverage.note: Implemented and unit-tested (23+ tests); obeyed in a real session: slice done refused (exit 5), release refused, stop still open.
gaps: Friction, not proof: a role with full Bash could allocate a terminal; no out-of-band secret
